subject: MSA + Order Form: liability carve-outs and SLA credits — coordination
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme redlines on liability & SLA — need legal review

Team — forwarding Acme's latest redline on the MSA and the parallel order form (attached). Highlights: they want the liability cap raised to 3x monthly charges and a carve-out for regulatory fines tied to PHI incidents; they are pushing back on the “credits are sole remedy” language for SLA when outages are repeated.

Immediate asks:
- Legal: can we accept 3x monthly in limited circumstances or propose a different metric?
- Sales/Deal: do we have flexibility to offer an exceptions carve-out for regulatory penalties (they say they need it for HIPAA exposure)?
- Ops: any operational levers we can commit to (SLOs, reporting cadence) that make a credit-only remedy more palatable?

I attached MSA_Acme_redline_v3.docx and OrderForm_Acme_v2.pdf.

Thanks — Sean

Attachments: MSA_Acme_redline_v3.docx (docx), OrderForm_Acme_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme redlines on liability & SLA — need legal review

Sean / team — quick read from Legal below. I kept it pragmatic to preserve the deal while protecting Redwood's exposure. Key recommendations:

1) Liability cap: We should hold the baseline global cap at the greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) USD 1,000,000. For order-form specific liability, propose a per-orderform monthly cap equal to 3x monthly charges but only for third-party direct damages arising out of the specific Order Form and excluding consequential damages.

2) Carve-outs: Carve out wilful misconduct, fraud, gross negligence, IP indemnity, and breaches of confidentiality/PHI from the cap. For regulatory fines arising from customer’s PHI, we should resist being contractually liable for regulatory penalties that are solely the customer's responsibility; however, we can accept indemnity for third-party claims and require notification/cooperation.

3) SLA / credits: Agree to keep credits as the sole monetary remedy for SLA failures but with two exceptions: (a) persistent systemic outages (defined as three separate incidents within a 30-day rolling window where aggregate downtime > 6 hours) and (b) breaches that are also confidentiality/PHI incidents (these already sit outside the cap). In exception (a) allow a limited uplift to the cap up to 3x monthly charges for that Order Form only.

4) Drafting pointers:
- Use explicit definitions ("Systemic Outage", "Confidentiality Breach") so the exception is operationally measurable.
- Remove any broad language that treats indemnity for regulatory fines as automatic; tie to customer-caused failures or Redwood's gross negligence/wilful misconduct.

I'll attach a redline snippet with suggested clause text. If Sales wants to soften the 3x uplift, I can draft alternative language (e.g., 2x for non-PHI events).

—Neha

Attachment: suggested_liability_snippet.txt (text)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Sep 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs and SLA credits (proposal)

Sam — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. We’ve reviewed internally and want to propose a compromise to keep the contracting timeline moving:

Summary of our proposal (high level):
- Baseline liability cap: greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000.
- Order Form uplift: for the Acme Order Form we will accept a limited uplift to 3x monthly charges but only in the narrow circumstance of a "Systemic Outage" (we define below). This uplift is a monetary cap for direct damages only and expressly excludes consequential damages.
- Carve-outs from cap: wilful misconduct, gross negligence, IP indemnity, and Confidentiality/PHI incidents.
- SLA remedy: service credits will remain the sole monetary remedy for SLA failures except where a Systemic Outage occurs (three incidents within a 30-day rolling period with aggregate downtime > 6 hours) or where an SLA failure is tied to a Confidentiality/PHI incident. In those cases the uplifted cap applies.

Rationale: this gives Acme a stronger remedy path for repeated, material reliability failures while keeping our enterprise exposure bounded and anchored to fees. For PHI/regulatory exposures we believe a carve-out is appropriate given potential statutory penalties, but we do not believe Redwood should accept direct responsibility for regulatory fines that result solely from the customer's own handling of PHI.

I’ve attached a single-document redline with the exact wording. Please have your counsel confirm the Systemic Outage definition and the carve-outs. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best — Ava

Attachments: MSA_Acme_redline_v3.docx (docx)

From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@acmehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Duncan Price <dprice@brockmanlaw.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs and SLA credits (proposal)

Ava — thanks for the quick response. A few points from Acme counsel and procurement:

1) Sole remedy carve-out: We appreciate the Systemic Outage definition, but we can’t accept an absolute sole-remedy rule for SLA failures that materially impact live patient workflows. If a systemic outage causes downstream regulatory reporting failures or patient harm (even if not a confidentiality breach), we need a path to additional remedies.

2) Regulatory fines: Our position is that if Redwood’s failure to follow applicable security/PHI controls contributes to a regulatory penalty (e.g., a HIPAA enforcement action that ties directly to Redwood's breach of the MSA obligations), Redwood should be contractually responsible for regulatory fines tied to that failure.

3) Cap quantum: 3x monthly charge for a systemic event is better than nothing, but given the scale of the Acme deployment we need a higher absolute floor. Can we set a minimum of USD 2,000,000 for events that involve PHI?

We can be pragmatic — if you accept a tailored carve-out for failures that are directly caused by Redwood (and not by Acme misconfiguration) and keep an explicit cooperation and forensic clause, we can consider the 3x uplift. Would prefer a call to run through a model scenario.

Sam

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — liability carve-outs and SLA credits (next steps)

Team — summary and proposed move:

1) For Acme we can accept:
   - Order Form uplift to 3x monthly charges for Systemic Outages (as defined).
   - Add absolute floor of USD 2,000,000 only when the event involves confirmed PHI exposure and is caused by Redwood's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. For non-PHI systemic outages keep the uplift without the 2M floor.

2) Regulatory fines: Resist blanket acceptance. Instead offer indemnity for third-party claims and agree to reimburse reasonable regulatory penalties if (and only if) they directly result from Redwood's material breach of security obligations and following an independent forensic report that attributes cause to Redwood. Require customer cooperation in the investigation.

3) SLA sole remedy: Keep credit-as-sole-monetary-remedy for standard SLA failures, but explicitly carve out Systemic Outages and PHI confidentiality incidents as exception triggers.

4) Ask Legal to produce a 1-page summary and clean redline (I asked Neha) with the exact conditional language.

If Sales is comfortable with the PHI floor caveat and the forensic trigger for fines, I recommend we present this to Acme tomorrow and schedule a 30-min call with their counsel and ours.

—Monica

P.S. Ops: can we prepare the incident taxonomy and monitoring reports format to attach to the Order Form so "Systemic Outage" is operationally defined?
